title: Apply for a conveyancer licence – corporation
summary: This page explains the requirements and process for a corporation to apply for a conveyancer licence to conduct legal work for property transactions.
intro:
For your company to do legal work for property transactions such as a sale or lease of land or the granting of a mortgage you need to apply for a conveyancer licence. You can apply for a licence online.

This licence requirement does not apply to an incorporated legal practice or solicitor corporation such as a law firm.
who_can_apply: Be a fit and proper person to hold a licence.
Not be a 'disqualified person' under the Conveyancers Licensing Act 2003.
Have at least one director who holds a current individual conveyancer licence.
Nominate a licensee in charge at each place of business that holds a current individual conveyancer licence.
Be considered fit and proper to hold a licence.
Pay the relevant contribution to the Property Services Compensation Fund.
Each director of the corporation must meet the requirements.
what_you_need: Copies of 2 proof of identity documents (PDF or JPG format) for all other company directors and the company secretary, if applicable.
The following forms completed and ready for uploading in PDF or JPG format: your fee payment.

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to apply for a conveyancer licence.
Download and complete the Application for a corporation conveyancer licence – PDF.
Gather the required supporting documents as indicated on the form.
Submit your application at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: Does this licence apply to all legal work for property transactions?
faqs.a: No, this licence requirement does not apply to an incorporated legal practice or solicitor corporation such as a law firm.

faqs.q: How can I check if an individual conveyancer licence is current?
faqs.a: You can check a conveyancer licence number and details at Verify NSW.

faqs.q: What is required for the corporation to be eligible?
faqs.a: The corporation must have at least one director who holds a current individual conveyancer licence, nominate a licensee in charge at each place of business who holds a current individual conveyancer licence, and meet mandatory insurance and fund contribution requirements.
